title: Recursive normalized coefficient transport for completed operation expressions
statement: Fix a coefficient datum and normalized family transport presentation $T$ as in [def-pur-completed-coefficient-family-transport-models]. Use the recorded finite input/unit/tensor/pullback expressions and their parenthesis-preserving substitution [def-pur-completed-operation-expressions], and the structural-map constructors of [def-pur-completed-operation-comparison-data]. Define $V_R(P)$ and $V_A(P)$ on families of complete objects recursively by input projection, the specified completed coefficient unit, completed tensor, and the specified completed pullback, with the same parentheses as $P$. Define the iterated coefficient comparison $e_P:V_A(P)(UM)\simeq U V_R(P)(M)$ recursively: identity at an input, the strong monoidal coefficient-unit map at a unit, tensor of the two recursive comparisons followed by the strong restriction tensorator at a tensor vertex, and completed constant pullback of the recursive comparison followed by the specified $b$ at a pullback vertex. Thus the tensor vertex is exactly the inverse-$a$ comparison under the recorded completed tensor identifications. Define $s_R,s_A$ for simultaneous substitution by the same identity/tensor/pullback recursion. Define $c_R(\alpha),c_A(\alpha)$ for each structural expression map by the specified associators, left/right unitors, symmetry, pullback-composition constraints, and functorial inverses/composites/tensor and pullback contexts. Define the substitution-transport predicate by $e_{P(\sigma)}\,U(s_R)=s_A\,V_A(P)(e_{\sigma})\,e_P$, for all expressions, all substitutions and all complete input families. Define the structural-transport predicate by $c_A(\alpha)\,e_Q=e_P\,U(c_R(\alpha))$ for every structural map $\alpha:P\to Q$ and every complete input family. These are concrete recursive constructions and predicates, without an existence assertion. Define the recursive ambient identification $V_R(P)\simeq\mathrm{completedValue}(P)$ by the reflected tensor identification at tensor vertices, the normalized pullback identification at pullback vertices, identity at inputs and the system-unit comparison at unit vertices.
